dataset.name: Raw seedling and sapling census data collected from June 2015 - April 2019 within a tropical wet forest in Puerto Rico
description: This data package contains data used to evaluate the effects of experimental warming (4˚C above ambient), drought, and hurricane disturbance on species richness, diversity, and composition of understory plant communities across ontogeny at the Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Experiment (TRACE) in Luquillo, Puerto Rico. The raw data in this package include a file for the species composition matrix of woody seedlings (>10 cm and <20 cm height; TRACE_composition_seedling.csv) and saplings (>20 cm height; TRACE_composition_sapling.csv) within the six TRACE plots, collected during six census dates from June 2015 to April 2019. Also included is also a file with the species names associated with the species codes found in the composition files (TRACE_species_codes.csv), and a data dictionary file describing the columns in the composition files (data_dictionary_composition_files.csv). All data files are in csv format, with the exception of the metadata which is in xml format.

spatialCoverage.description: These data were collected inside the six 12m^2 hexagonal plots of the Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Experiment (TRACE). TRACE is located in the Luquillo Experimental Forest (LEF), a subtropical we forest in northeastern Puerto Rico. Three of the experimental plots were warmed with infrared heaters by 4˚C higher than ambient temperature during part of the study, which the other three served as control. The plots were established in 2015 in a secondary forest located at ~100 m elevation, with a mean annual temperature of 24˚C and a mean annual rainfall of 3500 mm.

measurementTechnique:
All woody seedlings (>10 cm and <20 cm height) and saplings (>20 cm height) inside the TRACE experimental plots were tagged and identified to species in June 2015 (Census 0; C0), during the peak of a drought. Tagged seedlings were reassessed for drought damage in November 2015 (C1), after the rains resumed. The following censuses were conducted in June 2016 (C2; control year, 10 months after the drought ended), June 2017 (C3; 8 months after the warming started), May 2018 (C4; 7 months after the hurricanes Irma and María, in the absence of warming), and April 2019 (C5; 7 months after warming resumed and 14 months after the hurricanes). Seedlings that surpassed 20 cm height in a census year were reclassified as saplings. Additional details about the seedling censuses can be found in Bachelot et al. (2020), and more information about the experimental design of TRACE can be found in Kimball et al. (2018).
